title: WHY FLAMINGOS FEED UPSIDE DOWN
caption: That upside-down beak is a feeding tool! 🦩 #Flamingo #AnimalBehavior #NatureFacts #Wildlife #WildVox

narration_timeline.text: Why do these greater flamingos gather in crowds, then dip their faces into the water?
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic flock of greater flamingos, establishing the group before cutting to feeding.

narration_timeline.text: Watch one bird in the shallows. It's searching for tiny food, not just taking a drink.
narration_timeline.scene: Greater flamingo lowering its bill into shallow water, feeding.

narration_timeline.text: It turns its bill upside down and sweeps through the water as it feeds.
narration_timeline.scene: Greater flamingos actually dipping bills and moving in shallow water.

narration_timeline.text: Inside that unusual bill, comb-like edges help filter small organisms from the water.
narration_timeline.scene: Close real greater flamingo beak/head; anatomical filter is explained, not fabricated.

narration_timeline.text: While one bird feeds, others keep dipping, stepping, and searching around it.
narration_timeline.scene: Greater flamingos feeding or walking while searching in shallow water.

narration_timeline.text: So that strange head-down pose is a feeding tool. The flamingo's beak works like a living strainer.
narration_timeline.scene: Finish on a flock visibly dipping beaks to feed, resolving the upside-down-bill hook.
